{{Quote|If you can bribe a member of Bespin's Wing Guard into taking you on a spin around Cloud City, you won't regret spending the credits. The views are stunning.|Excerpt from ''[[Ullok's Underground Guide to Bespin]]''|<ref name="TNEGtVaV" />}}
The '''Storm IV Twin-Pod Cloud Car''' was an atmospheric vehicle known as a [[Cloud car/Legends|cloud car]] which was designed and manufactured by [[Bespin Motors/Legends|Bespin Motors]] on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].

==Description==
[[File:Cloudcar_schem.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Cloud car [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
This high-atmospheric aircraft consisted of two armored pods connected by a strong engine block housing the small yet powerful [[Kyromaster ion engine/Legends|Kyromaster]] dual ion engine system and the secondary [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] systems.<ref name="FF" /> The ion engine operated as the cloud-car's main propulsion system and allowed it to attain speeds of up to 1,500 kph while the repulsorlift drive was used for difficult maneuvers and increased the car's speed.<ref name="BtM" /> Much of the engine area was exposed to reduce engine heat and allow maximum air-cooling. As it was designed solely for atmospheric flight, the vehicle also had a system of flaps, jets, vanes, and rudders to improve control.

Both of the cloud car's pods contained a cockpit. The pilot was seated in the left pod, while gunner manned the right pod. The pilot's pod was equipped with advanced navigational systems and a communications array, while the gunner manned a pair of twin [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannons]]. Although not outfitted for advanced life support, the vehicle had pressurized cockpits for high-altitude flight and it was able to achieve low orbit using its repulsorlift system.

Though the weapons emplacements could hold a wide range of weapons, most of the original vehicles had a small power generator which limited it to supporting blaster cannons. Although inferior to the more powerful [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], the cloud car's cannons allowed it to take on starships such as the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].

==History==
[[File:Storm_IV_Cloud_Car_EotECR.png|thumb|right|220px|A cloud car modified for use on an icy planet]]
The Storm IV Twin-Pod Cloud Car was the first high-atmospheric aircraft to be categorized as a [[Cloud car/Legends|cloud car]].<ref name="AOR CRB">[[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> It was designed and produced by [[Bespin Motors/Legends|Bespin Motors]] to patrol the skies surrounding the floating mining colony and gambling resort [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]]. The Storm IV was originally employed by the [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Bespin Wing Guard]], who were responsible for the security of Cloud City.<ref name="BFI guide">[[Star Wars Battlefront: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Battlefront'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> The craft were originally designed to transport civilians, and were highly maneuverable.<ref name="RS II guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref>

When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Occupation of Bespin|occupied]] Cloud City in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] shortly after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], Bespin Motors began selling the vehicle to other markets. Thus, the Storm IV and other cloud car designs could be found across the galaxy on other worlds such as [[Taloraan/Legends|Taloraan]] as both civilian and military vehicles.<ref name="RSI">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref> The Storm IV was still in use on Cloud City as late as [[36 ABY]].<ref name="DNII">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MCQ-cloudcar.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Concept art by Ralph McQuarrie]]
The Storm IV cloud car first appeared with the release of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. The [[2004]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]'' depicts the Storm IV as a Fighter-Bomber armed with rockets like the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE Bomber]] and the [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-Wing]], though this may be game mechanics.

In the mission "Raid on Bespin" for the game ''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader'', the player has the option of switching their craft for a Storm IV Twin-Pod cloud car during the second objective.

In the Battlefront series games, the Storm IV is known only by the vague name of "Cloud Car". It is depicted as having poor acceleration and long takeoff time, although being capable of attaining extremely fast speeds and incredible turning capability. It is also armed with rockets in the games, although no launching apparatus is visible.
